---
title: "restore and get"
---

`proj restore` brings back the raw inputs a checked-out build used. `proj get local`
and `proj get github` copy directories from another analysis's build. Both follow
projr 0.9 (`projr_restore()`, `projr_get_local()`, `projr_get_github()`,
SATVILab/projr@5f915ef `R/restore-build.R`, `R/get.R`, `R/get-install.R`,
`R/get-project.R`) and share one download path. Every file is checked against the
build's manifest (MD5 per file) before any destination changes.

## proj restore

```bash
proj restore                               # every raw directory, GitHub "archive"
proj restore --label raw-data,raw-ref      # selected labels (repeat or comma-separate)
proj restore --version 1.2.0               # an older build
proj restore --destination reports         # a registered GitHub remote title
proj restore --destination v1.2.0-data     # a concrete Release tag in this repository
proj restore --destination local:backup    # a registered local remote (projcli only)
proj restore --clear                       # replace local changes
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--label` | every declared label starting with `raw` | Labels to restore. With no raw label, restore does nothing. |
| `--version` | the checkout's version | An exact build version, with or without `v`. |
| `--destination` | `archive` | A registered GitHub title, a concrete Release tag, or `local:<title>`. `github:<title>` names a GitHub title explicitly. |
| `--clear` | off | Allow replacing local files that differ from the build, including extra files. |
| `--profile` | the projr profile order | Profiles for the checkout's configuration. |
| `--max-bytes` | 2 GiB | Largest GitHub asset downloaded. |
| `--max-expanded-bytes` | 16 GiB | Largest expanded ZIP. |

The version is the checkout's `VERSION` when it names a completed build. On a
development version, it is the newest completed production build recorded in
`.projr/attempts` (projr reads `.projr/BUILDLOG.md`; projcli also reads a projr
BUILDLOG when no attempt record exists).

The checkout's `.projr/manifests` store (or a projr-written root `manifest.csv`)
records each label's files at that version. A directory that already matches is
left alone and needs no network access. A recorded empty directory needs no
remote either. Other labels come from the destination:

- A registered GitHub title uses the Release its build recorded, so `@version`,
  `@uuid` and `@branch` tags resolve to the build's own Release. Without a record,
  the tag template is expanded with the build version and the checkout's branch;
  `@uuid` then fails.
- An unregistered name is a Release tag in the checkout's repository (its Git
  `origin`). Both its archive asset (`<label>-v<version>.zip`) and its latest
  asset (`<label>.zip`) are tried.
- `local:<title>` reads a registered local remote at its recorded path (or its
  path template with the recorded `@uuid`). projr restores only from GitHub; this
  is a projcli addition.

When the exact version's archive is missing, an archive of an earlier version
with the identical file list is used. A remote's own `manifests/` (or
`manifest.zip`) must agree with the checkout's snapshot ("Sources disagree"
otherwise); a Release without a manifest relies on the checkout's snapshot alone.
A snapshot found only at the remote is added to the checkout's manifest store. A
missing `VERSION` is written. Nothing else in the project changes.

## proj get local and proj get github

```bash
proj get local --path ../analysis --label output --out downloads
proj get local --remote backup --version 1.2.0
proj get github --repo owner/analysis@main --label raw-data
proj get github --repo owner/analysis --tag archive
proj get github --remote reports --version 1.2.0 --out downloads
```

Supply exactly one of `--path` (local) or `--repo` (GitHub) and `--remote`.
Each label goes to `<out>/<label>/` (`--out` defaults to the current directory).
Without `--label`, the labels recorded for the build are copied. Without
`--version`, the producer's completed build is used, else the remote's advertised
`Project:` version.

- `--path` must be the root of the producing analysis. Its own directories, its
  registered local remotes and the default `_archive` are searched, at their
  recorded destinations.
- `--repo owner/repo[@branch]` reads the producer's configuration, BUILDLOG,
  `VERSION` and manifests from one commit of the branch (default: the repository's
  default branch), then its registered GitHub remotes and `archive`.
- `--tag` reads one Release directly.
- `--remote` names a remote registered in the current project.

`--overwrite` allows replacing changed or extra files in the selected output
directories; matching files are kept either way. A destination inside the source
analysis or a local remote is an error.

## Guarantees and limits

- Every selected label is staged in a hidden `.projr-get-*` folder beside its
  destination and verified before the first destination is replaced. Replacement
  renames the old directory aside and the new one into place. If a later label
  fails, earlier labels are moved back; an original that cannot be moved back is
  kept and its path reported.
- A destination that changed while restoring stops the restore before anything
  is replaced.
- Links and special files are rejected in sources and destinations. GitHub
  transfers are bounded, extracted privately and checked for unsafe ZIP members.
  Tokens never appear in errors and are not sent on download redirects.
- Restore and get only read remotes. They do not lock the output directory
  against other writers, and they are not crash-atomic.
- A local remote using `structure: latest` with `path-append-label: false` is not
  read. projcli producers' attempt records are not read over the GitHub API, so
  `--repo` without `--tag` resolves recorded destinations only from a projr
  BUILDLOG.
- `build.source` fetching (`proj source`) is a later slice.

Explicit CAS and Xet snapshots use `proj remote restore --title T --snapshot ID`
([remote](remote.qmd)).
